summary: Overall glucose management is fair with 86% time in range, but several severe hypoglycemic events (nadir 41–42 mg/dL) and missing carbohydrate entries limit optimization. The profile settings appear largely appropriate except for overly permissive automation safety limits. The primary opportunity is to begin logging all meals and to reduce the max IOB and max basal limits to safer, physiology-based values. Profile basal, targets, CR, ISF, and DIA are kept unchanged until meal data become available to separate basal from post-prandial patterns.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage 98.7%, 3995 valid entries, no invalid or duplicate data, 10 gaps with the largest 65 minutes. Nightscout telemetry is complete with treatments, device statuses, and events. No carbohydrate entries were recorded.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 entries, 98.7% coverage, good status, 10 gaps, largest 65 min, 0 duplicate or invalid entries, no carb records.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing carbohydrate entries limits meal-related assessment.

analysis_steps.findings: Moderate hypoglycemia burden with severe lows ≤45 mg/dL on three days. Time below range is 5.1%, mainly in late afternoon and early morning. Hyperglycemia peaks up to 293 mg/dL but time above range only 8.9%.
analysis_steps.evidence: Severe lows on 13 Aug (42 mg/dL), 14 Aug (41 mg/dL), 21 Aug (42 mg/dL). TBR 5.1%, TAR 8.9%, average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, CV 32.6%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No notable data gaps for safety assessment.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal likely adequate (hourly means 90–110 mg/dL) although hour 1 local shows 18.5% TBR. Late afternoon (15:00–18:00) hyperglycemia (average 148–162 mg/dL, TAR up to 32.1%) could be due to insufficient basal, unlogged meals, or other factors. Daytime target of 100 mg/dL combined with basal drop at 16:00 needs re-evaluation after meal data become available.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose: 00:00–07:00 mean 90–110 mg/dL, 15:00–18:00 mean 148–162 mg/dL, TAR peak 32.1% at 16:00. Basal profile: 0.5 U/h 16:00–18:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate or activity data to separate basal insufficiency from post-prandial patterns.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios cannot be assessed without meal entries. ISF of 56 mg/dL/U appears optimistic; correction boluses frequently overshoot, contributing to hypoglycemia. DIA of 10 hours appears appropriate. Profile ISF should not be changed until meal data allow distinction between correction errors and IOB stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Example correction bolus on 14 Aug 16:20 (0.2 U from 234 mg/dL) dropped glucose to 56 mg/dL at 120 min, indicating higher sensitivity than profile ISF predicts. Dynamic ISF values range from 27.8 to 111.9 mg/dL/U.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing meal entries and exact IOB stacking prevent reliable ISF adjustment.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and active. The combination effectively blunts hyperglycemia but can contribute to insulin stacking, especially without meal/COB gates. The current configuration is aggressive but not solely responsible for hypos.
analysis_steps.evidence: Loop logs show frequent SMB doses (0.05–0.4 U) and UAM boosts up to 35.93. SMB always enabled overrides COB-related gating.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal bolus logs to quantify stacking risk.

analysis_steps.findings: Max IOB of 25 U and max basal of 12 U/h are far above current usage (peak IOB ~5.9 U, peak temp basal ≤4 U/h) and pose a latent safety risk. These limits should be reduced to physiological safe ceilings. Dynamic ISF at 70% damping effectively compensates for ISF mismatches and is appropriate.
analysis_steps.evidence: Peak observed IOB 5.935 U, maximum enacted temp basal 4 U/h. Current profile total daily insulin ≈19.7 U. Suggested safe limits: max IOB 5 U, max basal 4 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: No declared meal strategy and no carbohydrate entries exist. The system relies on UAM to deliver insulin for unannounced meals, which complicates all other assessments.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0 carb entries, 0 carb boluses, no meal-related treatments. Telemetry shows only correction and temp basal activity.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb usage or extended absorption events observed. Default absorption parameters are untested.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0 e-carb entries; min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min, meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h are defaults.

analysis_steps.findings: The highest-priority action is to start logging all carbohydrates and declare a simple meal strategy. This unlocks future optimization of CR, ISF, and basal. Concurrently, the safety limits (max IOB, max basal) should be reduced to physiological values to protect against rare but possible over-delivery. Profile basal, targets, CR, ISF, and DIA should remain unchanged until meal data allow separation of basal, correction, and post-prandial patterns.
analysis_steps.evidence: No carb data blocks meal-related assessments; safety limits are excessively high (max IOB 25 U vs. 5.9 U peak; max basal 12 U/h vs. 4 U/h peak).

strengths: High CGM data quality (98.7% coverage, no invalid entries) provides a reliable foundation for analysis.
Time in range of 86% is commendable and exceeds many clinical targets.
Dynamic ISF adjustment effectively adapts to changing insulin sensitivity, smoothing out some profile mismatches.
issues: Severe hypoglycemic events (nadir 41–42 mg/dL) on three separate days indicate a safety risk that must be addressed.
Safety limits (max IOB 25 U, max basal 12 U/h) are set far above any observed need, creating a latent risk of excessive insulin delivery if an algorithm error occurs.

No carbohydrate entries exist, preventing evaluation of meal bolus timing, carb ratios, and post-prandial patterns; unannounced meals force the system to rely on UAM, which increases variability and stacking risk.

recommendations.title: Begin logging all carbohydrates and declare a meal strategy
recommendations.description: Without logged meals, the system cannot apply appropriate meal boluses, and all subsequent insulin adjustments are made in the dark. Implement a simple meal strategy: prebolus 15 minutes, 100% immediate bolus, no e-carbs.

suggested_change.action: Log all carbohydrate intake in AAPS and declare a meal strategy with prebolus 15 min, 100% immediate bolus, and e-carbs disabled.

recommendations.title: Reduce max IOB and max basal limits to safe physiological ranges
recommendations.description: Current max IOB of 25 U and max basal of 12 U/h are far in excess of observed usage (peak IOB ~5.9 U, peak basal ≤4 U/h). These values should be lowered to 5 U IOB and 4 U/h basal to prevent accidental over-delivery while still allowing therapeutic dosing.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all basal segments unchanged. The late afternoon hyperglycemia may reflect insufficient 16:00–18:00 basal, but without meal logs this cannot be confirmed. Re-evaluate after 5–7 days of carbohydrate logging.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight basal appears adequate; afternoon hyperglycemia could be due to unlogged meals or other factors. Changing basal prematurely risks destabilizing safe overnight control.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log all carbohydrates for at least 5 days, then review glucose trends between 15:00 and 18:00. If hyperglycemia persists without a meal contribution, consider increasing the 16:00–18:00 basal by 0.1–0.2 U/h.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits are excessively high relative to actual insulin usage, posing a latent safety risk. Reducing them to physiological safe ceilings (max basal to 4 U/h, max IOB to 5 U) maintains therapeutic headroom while preventing accidental overdosing.
Dynamic ISF effectively compensates for variable sensitivity; 70% damping is a reasonable starting point. No change needed.
Defaults are acceptable; no meal data to evaluate performance.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Declare a simple meal strategy: prebolus 15 minutes, 100% immediate bolus, no extended carbs. Log all carbohydrates promptly.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: No carbohydrate entries currently exist, making meal-related insulin delivery invisible. Adopting a standard prebolus and immediate bolus approach, together with consistent logging, is the first step to enabling future optimization of carb ratios and post-prandial control.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log at least 5–7 days of meals with consistent prebolus timing, then examine post-prandial glucose excursions and correction requirements.

implementation_steps: 1. Begin logging all carbohydrate intake in AAPS immediately; do not skip any meal or snack.
2. Under meal settings, set prebolus to 15 minutes and ensure e-carbs are disabled. Use 100% immediate bolus for all meals.
3. Navigate to AAPS safety settings and change max_iob_units from 25 to 5, and max_basal_u_per_hour from 12 to 4.

4. After collecting at least 5 days of carbohydrate data, review glucose trends between 15:00 and 18:00. If hyperglycemia persists without a preceding meal, consider a small increase in the 16:00–18:00 basal segment.

5. Once meal data are available, evaluate correction bolus outcomes. If hypos post-correction continue even without meal influence, reduce ISF from 56 mg/dL/U to a lower value (e.g., 40–48 mg/dL/U) after discussing with the care team.
education: Logging all carbohydrate intake is essential for closed-loop systems; unannounced meals force the algorithm to react to hyperglycemia rather than prevent it, increasing variability.
Safety limits in AAPS act as hard caps on insulin delivery. Setting them close to actual maximum needs prevents accidental large doses while still allowing the system to treat hyperglycemia.
The dynamic ISF feature adjusts insulin sensitivity in real time. Keeping it enabled with a damping factor of 70% helps smooth out day-to-day sensitivity changes without abrupt dose swings.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support only; all suggested changes must be reviewed and verified by the user. Make one change at a time and monitor glucose closely after each adjustment.

A severe hypoglycemic event (≤54 mg/dL) requires immediate treatment and a review of recent insulin delivery. After any safety limit reduction or meal strategy change, pay extra attention overnight for several days.
Do not change multiple profile settings simultaneously; separate basal, ISF, and automation adjustments by at least 3–5 days of observation.
